name: Manchester United 1995/96
scopeNote: Style not established: sources support only a 4-4-2-family shape in general terms (Wilson, on Ferguson's sides across the 1990s, not this season) and a youth-led squad rebuild (Premier League review, Wikipedia). Period 1995-08-19 (Aston Villa 1-3, first match) to 1996-05-11 (FA Cup final 1-0 Liverpool); league clinched 1996-05-05. Tactical dimensions have no period-specific verified source; they are gaps, not evidence of absence. Second pass: Hansen/Goal pieces add Ferguson using Hansen's remark to motivate the squad (secondary paraphrase) and the opening-day line-up only; still no season-wide tactical source (Spielverlagerung/TFT/Coaches' Voice searches returned nothing).

sources.title: 1995/96 Season Review
sources.evidence: United surprised by "selling established first-team trio Paul Ince, Andrei Kanchelskis and Mark Hughes" with no major signings; Ferguson "threw a host of academy stars into the fold" (Beckham, Scholes, the Nevilles, Butt became regular starters). Hansen on Match of the Day: "You can't win anything with kids." Title won by four points.

sources.title: 1995-96 Manchester United F.C. season
sources.evidence: First 100k chars read. "Having started the season without a major summer signing"; only summer arrival Nick Culkin (York City). Ferguson "drafted in young players like Nicky Butt, David Beckham, Paul Scholes" and the Nevilles, paired with veterans Bruce, Keane, Schmeichel. First match 1995-08-19 Aston Villa (a) 1-3; league clinched 1996-05-05 Middlesbrough (a) 3-0; last match FA Cup final 1996-05-11 Liverpool 1-0. Page has no tactics.

sources.title: Sir Alex Ferguson was as adept at evolving tactically as any manager in history (Jonathan Wilson, Guardian News Service)
sources.evidence: Ferguson's sides "had always been part of the 4-4-2 family" before the 2000 shift. Career-wide, not specific to 1995/96, so context only; no pressing/marking content.

sources.title: Alan Hansen's 'You Can't Win Anything With Kids' Comment & Man Utd's 1995 Thumping at Aston Villa
sources.evidence: Opening-match line-up only (Aston Villa 1-3): "Butt partnered Roy Keane in midfield"; "Scholes played off the front with veteran Scottish forward Brian McClair." Also "four players aged 20 or younger" (G. Neville, P. Neville, Butt, Scholes); "Potential aside, it was a huge gamble from Ferguson". One match, not a season-wide system.

sources.title: You can't win anything with kids: Alan Hansen's infamous Man Utd rant and the aftermath (Goal)
sources.evidence: Ferguson "often went back to Hansen's comments to motivate his side throughout the season" (article paraphrase, no direct Ferguson quote). Hansen later: "The kids were great, but so were the goalkeeper, two centre-backs and the centre forward."

confidence.reason: Squad-building verified (Premier League review, Wikipedia); people-management and opening-day shape only from secondary tier C pieces (SI, Goal); no season-wide tactical analysis or direct Ferguson quote found.
